description: Actual design token VALUES for the Vois token set — distinct from data/vois-rules.json, which holds the constraints that govern how tokens are used. Sourced from vois-tokens/references/*.md.

spacing_scale.description: All spacing must be divisible by 4 or 8. The scale is the Figma Spacing variables (--space-{px}); the semantic spacing tokens (--space-padding-*, --space-v-*, --space-h-*) alias it.

levels.use: Page title. Once per screen only.
Named items, modal titles, core actions
Short descriptions in toasts, alerts, dialogs, popovers

type_scale.note: Font choice itself is workspace-specific — always reference the token, never a font name directly (DS-TYPOGRAPHY-005).

usage_table.when_to_use: Elements that change state while staying on screen (progress bars, toggles)
Constant-speed loops only — marquees, spinners, hold-to-delete

custom_curves.attribution: Benjamin De Cock, used in Linear

elevation_tiers.description: Five tiers, from the Figma effect styles (Elevation/*). Don't invent a sixth. Use the token, never the shadow value. The registry's vois-tokens item ships each tier's layers as CSS.

tiers.use: A raised card (in the page), a dropdown menu (dropdown layer)

surface_border_shadow.description: Three-layer shadow acting as a 1px border + lift + ambient depth, used in place of solid borders on cards/containers that show depth.

sizes.use: Inline with body/label text, inside inputs
Inline with H4/H5 text, default button icon
Empty states, feature callouts, large standalone icons

color.note: Token names are the Figma variables' Web code syntax (references/figma-variables.md). Components read System and Component tokens (these examples), never a Global palette step such as --blue-9. Default values for every color variable, in light and dark, ship as the registry's vois-tokens item (ommakes/Skills, registry/vois/tokens/vois-tokens.css), generated from Figma with a generic blue brand. A workspace's own values replace them.

status_roles.status: names fixed by Figma; defaults in the registry's vois-tokens item
status_roles.note: This repo fixes the role and token names so every component reads the same ones. The default values, light and dark, ship as the registry's vois-tokens item. A workspace that sets its own sets them in :root and .dark (not @theme, DS-TOKEN-003), or in defineVars, with a light and a dark value, and checks the pairs against contrast_minimums (DS-A11Y-004). Foreground on surface is normal text (4.5:1). Border and base color against the page are UI components (3:1).

info.meaning: Neutral context or a tip. Nothing is wrong and nothing succeeded.

negative.meaning: An error, a failure, a blocked state, or a destructive action.

notice.meaning: Caution, or something that needs attention before it becomes an error. This is the warning level, not an error.

breakpoints.note: Use em for hand-authored @media queries, not px, so breakpoints respect the user's browser font-size preference. Tailwind's built-in breakpoints use px internally and are unaffected.

touch_target_minimum.note: Sets the minimum click or tap target area only. It never sets the visual size of a button, icon, or control. Exempt from the 4 and 8 spacing scale because it measures a target, not spacing.

widths.note: rem so widths respect the user's browser font size, matching the em breakpoints (DS-CSS-007).

tokens.use: Form container ceiling. Also the ceiling for textareas.
Default ceiling for a single-line field.
Short fixed-format values: postal code, state code, expiry, security code.
Narrowest viewport layouts must support without horizontal scroll.
Small dialog ceiling: confirmations, AlertDialogs, typed confirmation, single-column content.
Large dialog ceiling: a textarea or content that needs the extra width. Dialogs are always single column.
Minimum click or tap target area. Never sets visual size. See tokens.json_edits.

table_sizes.note: rem so table sizes respect the user's browser font size. --table-offset and --app-header-h are not tokens: each page sets them (DS-TABLE-019).

tokens.use: Header row height. Also the scroll-padding-block-start and the sticky offset.
Dense row height. Pointer devices only.
Regular row height. Matches --hit-area-min, so rows are tappable.
Starting height of a form textarea, in text lines
Height at which a form textarea stops growing and scrolls
Starting height of an AI chat input
Height at which a chat input stops growing and scrolls

grid_and_panels.status: DEFAULT. These are the default Vois values for grid and panels. They match vois-tokens/scripts/grid-fixture.json, and grid.test.mjs checks the two agree. If your token source defines different values, use those and update the fixture.

--grid-margin-min-at.status: new, window width where the margin is at its minimum

--grid-margin-max-at.status: new, window width where the margin reaches its maximum

--grid-gutter-min-at.status: new, region width where the gutter is at its minimum

--grid-gutter-max-at.status: new, region width where the gutter reaches its maximum

--grid-margin.status: output, built from the four --grid-margin tokens. Not stored.

--grid-gutter.status: output, built from the four --grid-gutter tokens. Not stored.

--region-right-rail.status: new, proposed, not in the template text

--region-filters.status: new, proposed, not in the template text

--region-company-facts.status: new, proposed, not in the template text

--region-contents.status: new, proposed, not in the template text

--region-buy-box.status: new, from the product template text

--region-subnav.status: new, from the settings template text

--measure-feed.status: new, from the feed template text

--measure-settings.status: new, from the settings template text

--measure-article.status: new, from the article and case study text

--measure-onboarding.status: new, from the onboarding template text
